thread:
maya: Quick sync — continuous-batching tuning for the embeddings / reranker endpoints (non-chat workloads). Seeing intermittent tail spikes when the batcher targets a token budget before flushing. Want to propose queue policy adjustments and token-budget targets. Thoughts?

sam: Can you paste the recent profiling snapshot? curious whether kernels or queueing latency is the dominant factor.

maya: P95 spikes mostly coming from queueing, not GPU kernels. Profiling from yesterday: average kernel time per token is steady, but waiting-for-batch time jumps when traffic is bursty. I attached a short summary:
```
- model: reranker-xl (2B)
- request size: avg 64 tokens (text concat of pair)
- baseline (old heuristic): token_budget_target=2048, max_wait_ms=25, max_batch_size=64
- observed: P95 queue_wait ~120ms on 99th percentile bursts, overall P95 end-to-end ~310ms
```

anya: Hmm. For non-chat rerank/embedding workloads we should favor count-based batching for embeddings (many tiny requests) and token-budget for long-decoder workloads. Reranker sits in-between. Suggest: separate logical queues: `embeddings` and `reranker`. Each queue gets its own flush policy.

devon: Agreed. For embeddings: prefer small fixed batch size with short max_wait (e.g., batch_size=128, max_wait_ms=10) because token lengths ~ < 64 and kernel setup amortizes. For reranker: use hybrid: min_batch_count=8 OR token_budget_target=1024 OR max_wait_ms=20. That avoids waiting too long for big tokens.

sam: +1. Also consider a "fast-path" for single-request flush: if queue depth=1 and estimated kernel throughput indicates GPU will be underutilized, flush immediately to keep latency low. Could be a simple heuristic: if queued_tokens < 128 and gpu_util < 30% => flush.

maya: I ran an A/B yesterday with these params (reranker hybrid). Short summary:
```
A (baseline): token_budget=2048, p95=310ms, p99=690ms, throughput 1.0x
B (hybrid): min_count=8, token_budget=1024, max_wait=20ms -> p95=200ms, p99=380ms, throughput 0.98x
Notes: embeddings queue moved to count-based: batch_size=256, max_wait=12ms -> p95=90ms, p99=160ms, +1.1x throughput
```

maya: The tradeoff was small throughput dip for reranker but big tail improvements. We also saw fewer kernel-switch events because batches were more size-stable which improved kernel selection consistency.

anya: Nice. Did the profiler show KV cache churn increases? reranker sometimes hits attention mask patterns that cause cache inflation.

maya: KV churn was minimal for these workloads — most requests don't reuse caches (stateless reranker). But we observed less cache pressure when batch sizes were stable because memory allocation patterns were more predictable.

devon: One operational concern: if we split queues, scheduler needs to ensure fair GPU shares. Embeddings can saturate and starve reranker. We should add per-queue burst tokens and a simple round-robin drain with weights. Eg weights {embeddings:0.6, reranker:0.4}.

sam: Also ensure the fallback policy when load is high: auto-fallback to smaller model or quantized variant. For reranker, a 4-bit quantized reranker-lite is acceptable if latency otherwise spikes. That ties into smart routing.

maya: Implementation plan proposal:
- create two logical queues at the runtime layer (embeddings, reranker)
- embeddings: count-based batcher (default batch_size=256, max_wait_ms=12)
- reranker: hybrid batcher (min_count=8, token_budget=1024, max_wait_ms=20)
- add fast-path single flush heuristic (queued_tokens<128 && gpu_util<30%)
- scheduler: weighted round-robin with per-queue burst tokens and cap per-second
- metric hooks: track queue_wait_ms histogram per-queue, batch_size distribution, kernel-switch rate, kv-allocs

anya: Sounds good. Can we add a feature flag and rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% with canary monitors for p95/p99 and throughput?

maya: Yes. Will add rollout plan + alerting thresholds: if p99 increases >20% or throughput drops >10% rollback.

perf-bot: perf/regression check queued. Running synthetic harness: 10k/s mixed embeddings/reranker traffic. Expected: p95_end2end reduction ~30% for embeddings, ~35% for reranker.

devon: One more tweak: for reranker, when a request contains many candidate pairs (n>32), treat as multi-req internally and limit per-batch candidate sum to 1024 tokens to avoid one request monopolizing the batch.

maya: Good call. I'll add per-request token cap with controlled splitting.

sam: Who wants to own the patch? I can take the runtime changes (batcher + fast-path). Anya can do scheduler weighting and rollout automation. Devon will add per-request splitting. Maya will own perf dashboards & canary config.

anya: I'll add the alerting rules to the rollout PR.

maya: Great — I'll open an RFC PR with the configs + perf snapshots. Target to land canary next Wed. Thanks all :rocket: 

devon: 👍

sam: Thanks, will start on a branch today.
